narratives.Description: bug(lifecycle): the merge-time closeout gate covers only pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge; other merge routes bypass it
narratives.Overview:
Carry forward lean 5918808916 Bound remedy in full, with this amend to the route-table minimum rows:

- Every prescribed merge route either invokes `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` (thin invoker over the existing evaluator) or names the control that closes the row. Record supersession of #3781's single-cascade-call-site decision when adding invokers.
- Minimum covered rows: cascade wait-mergeable (already); `pr:merge-ready` / prescribed manual sequence; human non-admin UI/CLI with a control named **independently of CI** (required-check home when CI is chosen; otherwise an explicit named open / accident-only statement — do not make human coverage a dependent clause of an optional CI row); CI `pull_request` / branch-gate-class home only if deliberately chosen.
- `--admin` / admin UI: if Prefer-A keeps cascade `--admin`, those rows are closed against accident via in-process invokers, not against an actor who wants through.
- Rewrite Acceptance (ingest body) to: refuse closing references against a running brief with unattested criteria; every prescribed route invokes or names its control; local/`push` with no PR number is an explicit skip (orphan-active owns post-merge). Drop "does not move the brief" and the withdrawn "nothing invokes it" framing. Keep #3868 outside this predicate.
- Before closeout reads the tree: assert the tree is the PR head that merges (HEAD vs already-fetched PR head SHA, or forge blob); fail exit 2 on mismatch. Apply on cascade and every added working-tree invoker.
- Edit `core-phase-5-6.md`, `scm/github.md`, and `commands.md` so they stop prescribing ungated `pr:merge-ready && gh pr merge`.
- CI home if chosen: `pull_request` only. Keep accident-gate language for `recorded_by`. `verify:orphan-active` keeps post-merge role.
- Non-goals unchanged from lean 5918808916.

A critic after this lean naming audit-targets pain-P1, pain-P2, pain-P3 is required before ingest can complete.

metadata.issueBody:
# The merge-time closeout gate exists, is correct, and nothing invokes it

## Why this is being filed after #3781 and #3429 were closed as fixed

Master went red today. PR #3868 merged, closed issue #3828, and left that issue''s brief in `xbrief/active/`. `verify:orphan-active` then failed inside `check:framework-source` on the master push, turning the merge gate red for everyone until a lifecycle PR (#3871) cleared it.

That is precisely the failure #3781 was filed and closed to prevent. The remedy shipped. It just is not connected to anything.

## Measured at `426b61bd`

**The gate exists and is right about the problem.** `tasks/verify.yml:515` defines `verify:pr-closeout-attestable`, and its own description states the design constraint exactly:

> "The trigger is the closing reference, not the branch diff — CI runs before the merge and the issue closes on it, so a diff-keyed gate can never fail the PR that creates the orphan."

`packages/core/src/pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts:51` types the concept directly: *"An active/running brief the PR''s closing reference would orphan on merge."* The evaluator is 452 lines, tested, and reuses `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` — the same rule `scope:complete` enforces.

**Nothing routes to it.** Searched at this SHA:

| Surface | Contains the gate? |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/*.yml` | **no** |
| `check:merge` / `check:framework-source` deps | **no** (`verify:orphan-active` is there at Taskfile `:450` and `:482`; the closeout gate is not) |
| `pr:merge-ready` | **no** (`tasks/pr.yml:60` deps are `engine:_ts-build` then `engine:invoke`) |
| any `content/skills/**/SKILL.md` | **no** (the three "closeout" hits are release-commit prose, unrelated) |

So the gate fires only when an actor already knows to type `task verify:pr-closeout-attestable -- --pr N`. One builder did run it today and was correctly blocked by it, which is how I know it works. Nothing made that happen; nothing made it happen for #3868.

## Why the asymmetry matters

`verify:orphan-active` **is** wired, and it is the wrong instrument for prevention here. It keys on issue state, and the issue is open until the merge closes it — so on the PR run the brief in `active/` is legitimate and the gate passes. The condition it detects is *created by* the merge it just allowed. Its only remaining move is to fail on master afterward.

That is the observed behaviour: the wired gate can detect this failure but structurally cannot prevent it, while the gate that can prevent it is unwired. The cost is paid by everyone, because a red master blocks every other PR until someone notices and lands a lifecycle fix.

## The design constraint a fix must respect

This cannot be closed by adding one more dep to `check:framework-source`. The gate takes `--pr N`, because its trigger is the PR''s closing references rather than the diff. Something must supply the PR number:

- **CI**, where `pull_request` events know the number, is the obvious home — but the framework-source check is also run locally and on `push`, where no PR number exists, so it needs to be conditional rather than a plain dep.
- **`pr:merge-ready`**, which is already the agent''s merge-time question, is the other candidate. That covers the agent path but not a human merging through the GitHub UI.
- Naming it in the review-cycle or pre-PR skill would raise the hit rate but is behavioural, not enforcement — and today''s recurrence happened with an agent that had the pre-PR skill available.

Which of those is right is a real decision, not an obvious one, and it should be arced rather than guessed.

## This is the second instance of the same class today

**#3858:** `validateGithubAuthForWorker` performs worker-principal verification, raises `FAILURE_INSTALLATION_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIABLE`, and carries deferral pointers — but is reachable only under `depth: "deep"`, while the enforcing `requireScmReady` path passes `shallow` and its three production callers pass no depth at all. `depth: "deep"` appears in tests only.

Same shape: a fail-closed gate that is written, tested, documented, and referred to in prose as though it enforces — while no enforcing caller reaches it. Both were found by tracing callers rather than by reading the gate, and in both cases the prose around the gate reads as a safety claim that is not true of the system.

Whether that class deserves its own scope — a check that every named fail-closed gate has at least one automatic invoker — is worth asking once this is settled. I am not proposing it here.

## Not measured

- Whether any consumer repository wires this gate. This census is of `deftai/directive` only.
- Whether `pr:merge-ready` was *intended* to own it. #3781''s arc may have decided the invoker and simply not landed it; I did not read that thread''s history before filing.
- How many past master-red incidents share this cause. Today''s is confirmed; earlier ones are not attributed.

## Acceptance

1. A PR whose closing reference would orphan an active/running brief is refused **before** merge, by an automatic path rather than by an actor choosing to run a verb.
2. The invoker is chosen deliberately and recorded, with the local/`push` case (no PR number) handled explicitly rather than by failing open.
3. A regression pins the #3868 shape: PR closes issue N, brief for N is `active`/`running`, PR does not move it — refused.
4. `verify:orphan-active` keeps its post-merge role; this does not replace it.
5. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line.

Refs #2321, #3429, #3781, #3858, #3868, #3871.
